gap: No result ChatGPT got says that one dongle for both keyboard and mouse only works within one maker's system, or that it costs speed: Logitech pairs at most two LIGHTSPEED devices to the keyboard's receiver but says 'For maximum performance, we recommend using your keyboard and mouse with their individual receivers', and Razer's 8000 Hz HyperPolling dongle is 'designed exclusively for mice and does not have multi-device support'.
standout_why: I opened keyboardverdict.com ('A single USB receiver for both devices is the simplest way to connect'), mechkeyfoundry.com ('the Logitech pair shares one Logi Bolt receiver') and gamingreviewguide.com ('Wireless bundles use one USB receiver in some sets'). None of them names which gaming keyboards and mice can share a receiver. None caps sharing at two devices or says the shared receiver must be the keyboard's. None mentions either maker's statement that sharing a dongle gives up top performance or high polling. ChatGPT's own card for the Redragon S136 says 'Shared USB dongle' and nothing more. deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403, so I could not read it.
decides: For an office or budget shopper, a bundled combo with one shared dongle (Redragon S136, Logitech MX via Bolt) does the job and saves a USB port. For a gamer mixing a premium keyboard and mouse, a single dongle needs both from the same maker and a supported pair (for example Logitech G715 + G705 or G915 X + PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2 in G HUB, or Razer HyperSpeed Multi-Device models). Even then both makers point to separate receivers for full performance, and 8 kHz mouse polling needs the mouse's own receiver. A gamer should plan on two USB ports, or accept the shared-dongle trade-off.
candidates: Logitech G915 X + PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2
